mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has risen monotonically for three straight weeks (-48.4 to -44.6), indicating a steady recovery in commuting and errand-running activity that should translate into higher retail footfall as more people move through transit hubs near shops over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT continuing its upward trend, indicating decoupling of transit recovery from retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility exceeding 8 points (from -15.4 to -24.3) signals renewed restrictions or employer-driven work-from-home mandates, which would suppress adjacent lunchtime and after-work retail visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -15.4 to -24.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 2 weeks despite the WORKPLACES threshold breach, or WORKPLACES recovers within one week without retail impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS rebound (-24.6 to -9.6) combined with stable, slightly positive RESIDENTIAL readings suggests households are substituting outdoor leisure for indoor retail and recreation trips, jointly depressing RETAIL_REC over the coming week as the substitution effect outweighs any general mobility recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped 15 points in the latest week while RESIDENTIAL stayed flat
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week even as PARKS remains elevated and RESIDENTIAL stays flat, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-March marks the end of Australian summer holidays and school return, historically reducing discretionary retail and recreation trips as routines shift toward work and school commutes rather than leisure shopping, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2022-03-15 falls at the post-summer seasonal transition in Victoria
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite the seasonal transition, indicating the seasonal effect is dominated by other factors.

mechanism_narrative: The most recent week shows RETAIL_REC improving from -15.3 to -13.9, a reversal of the prior two-week decline, suggesting behavioral momentum is building that will carry RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as consumers resume deferred shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved week-on-week in the latest observation after two weeks of decline

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved while WORKPLACES dropped sharply in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite the WORKPLACES decline outweighing TRANSIT improvement, indicating TRANSIT dominance instead.
